player_action: I make a full attack against the orc, then take a 5-foot step away. Does the step provoke?
game_state: Fighter adjacent to two orcs, has not moved otherwise this round.
correct_ruling: A 5-foot step doesn't provoke and can be taken before, during, or after a full attack, as long as you take no other movement that round.
common_wrong_rulings: You must take the 5-foot step before the full attack.
The step provokes from the second orc.

player_action: I'm going to drop prone to make myself a smaller target for the archers. Does that provoke from the swordsman next to me?
game_state: Fighter adjacent to a swordsman, archers 60 ft away.
correct_ruling: Dropping prone is a free action and does not provoke an attack of opportunity. Prone gives +4 AC vs ranged attacks but -4 AC vs melee attacks.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Free Actions > Drop Prone; Conditions > Prone
common_wrong_rulings: Prone gives disadvantage on ranged attacks against you (5e).

player_action: I use my attack of opportunity to trip the orc that is fleeing.
game_state: Fighter with longsword (no Improved Trip) threatened by... orc moves away.
correct_ruling: An attack of opportunity is a melee attack, and trip can be attempted in place of a melee attack, so you may trip as an AoO; without Improved Trip, the trip attempt itself (the melee touch attack) provokes an AoO from the orc unless you have Improved Trip.
common_wrong_rulings: You can't trip on an AoO.
Trip is a contested Athletics check.
confidence_note: Whether a trip attempt made as an AoO itself provokes is a known gray area.

player_action: I attack the ogre with my longsword. The ogre's friend, a goblin, is also next to me. Does attacking provoke?
game_state: Fighter adjacent to ogre and goblin.
correct_ruling: A normal melee attack does not provoke an attack of opportunity.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Actions in Combat table (Attack (melee): no AoO)
common_wrong_rulings: Attacking one enemy provokes from the other.

player_action: I tumble past the hobgoblin to get behind it.
game_state: Rogue, Tumble +8, moving through hobgoblin's threatened area at half speed.
correct_ruling: A DC 15 Tumble check lets you move at half speed through threatened squares without provoking from that opponent; moving through an enemy's square requires DC 25. Failure means you provoke normally.

player_action: I tumble through the troll's square to get past it.
game_state: Rogue with Tumble +12, troll occupies the square.
correct_ruling: Tumbling through an enemy's square requires a DC 25 Tumble check (at half speed); if it fails you stop before entering the square and provoke as normal.
common_wrong_rulings: DC 15 to tumble through an occupied square.

player_action: I'm only moving 5 feet as part of my move action, so it's basically a 5-foot step and shouldn't provoke.
game_state: Fighter adjacent to an orc. He plans to move 5 ft away as a move action and then move another 20 ft with his standard action (a double move).
correct_ruling: Because he is moving more than 5 feet this round, the first 5 feet is ordinary movement, not a 5-foot step; leaving the orc's threatened square provokes. A 5-foot step is only possible in a round with no other movement.
common_wrong_rulings: Any movement of 5 ft never provokes.

player_action: I use the Sentinel feat so the orc's speed drops to 0 when I hit it with my AoO.
correct_ruling: There is no Sentinel feat in 3.5 SRD; that's a 5e feat. AoOs simply deal damage; to stop movement you'd use options like trip as the AoO (or Stand Still-type feats not in the SRD).

player_action: I activate my wand of magic missile next to the goblin.
correct_ruling: Activating a spell trigger item such as a wand is a standard action and does not provoke an attack of opportunity (unlike spell completion items such as scrolls, which provoke as spellcasting does).
srd_reference: MagicItems > Using Items > Spell Trigger; Actions in Combat table (Use spell-like ability / activate magic item)
common_wrong_rulings: Wands provoke just like casting the spell.
confidence_note: Fairly confident the SRD Spell Trigger text says it does not provoke; not checked against the text in this session.

player_action: I'm swinging from the chandelier past the orc's reach. Does that count as moving out of a threatened square?
game_state: Swashbuckling rogue, chandelier rope, orc below.
correct_ruling: Rules don't specifically cover swinging; movement out of threatened squares generally provokes regardless of the method, but the DM decides how the stunt resolves (e.g., a Jump/Tumble/Climb check and whether the orc can reach).
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Attacks of Opportunity > Provoking (movement); DM adjudication

player_action: The orc is blinded. I move away. Does it get an AoO?
correct_ruling: A blinded creature still threatens and can make AoOs, but every opponent has total concealment (50% miss) relative to it; and you can't make AoOs against an opponent with total concealment, so effectively no AoO.
srd_reference: Conditions > Blinded; CombatII.rtf > Concealment > Total Concealment
confidence_note: Interaction of blinded attacker vs total concealment rule for AoOs; likely no AoO but phrasing uncertain.

player_action: I'm going to load my heavy crossbow while the gnoll is next to me.
game_state: Fighter with heavy crossbow, adjacent gnoll.
correct_ruling: Loading a heavy crossbow is a full-round action that provokes attacks of opportunity.
srd_reference: Equipment > Weapons > Crossbow, heavy; Actions in Combat table (Load a heavy or repeating crossbow)

player_action: Total defense: can I still take attacks of opportunity?
correct_ruling: No — while in total defense you can't make attacks of opportunity; you get +4 dodge bonus to AC for 1 round.

player_action: I cast a quickened magic missile next to the orc. Does that provoke?
game_state: Wizard with Quicken Spell, adjacent orc.
correct_ruling: Casting a quickened spell does not provoke an attack of opportunity (the Quicken Spell feat says so). It is a free action and only one quickened spell may be cast per round.
common_wrong_rulings: Quickened spells provoke like normal casting.
